real_estate.homebuilder: Case-Shiller's August reading has the San Francisco metro, which includes Alameda County, up 3.4% from a year earlier, ahead of the nation's 2.1%.
real_estate.commentary:
Today's housing number is prices. The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller index for August, out this morning, has national home prices up 2.1% from a year earlier, up from 1.9% in July. The San Francisco metro index, which takes in Alameda County, is up 3.4% from a year earlier, though before seasonal adjustment it slipped 0.7% from July, the usual late summer cooling.

Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average held at 7.33% Monday and the 15-year is 6.99%, with Tuesday's reading due later today and the Fed's decision on Wednesday (more in Economy). Locally, inventory thinned: the board wide table fell to 2,578 from 2,623, with 144 coming soon and 185 brand new. The five city ledger slipped to 678 from 686, led by Union City at 61 from 65 and Hayward at 198 from 201, while Fremont (226), Newark (89) and Milpitas (104) moved by one each.

What this means for you: prices here are still rising, about 3.4% a year, but at 7.33% buyers have room to negotiate, so sellers should price for today's payment from day one. And if a client is weighing the Microsoft buyout in the Stocks section, have them talk to a lender before they sign.

• Board wide: 2,578 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 144 coming soon and 185 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 678 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 607 are on the market and 71 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 226 live, 181 active, 28 coming soon and 17 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,299,944 at $801 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 34 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 198, Milpitas 104, Newark 89, Union City 61.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,079,000 at $666 a square foot. 284 homes are priced under a million, and 184 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.note: Levels are Monday, October 26 at the closing bell. Live at 8:07 AM PT Tuesday: S&P 500 up 0.49%, Dow down 0.03%, Nasdaq up 0.97%.
stocks.news:
Stocks are mixed a day before the Fed: as of 8:07 AM PT the S&P 500 is up 0.49%, the Dow down 0.03% and the Nasdaq up 0.97%, after Monday's broad gain. Wednesday is a double feature: the Fed decides at 11 AM our time, and Microsoft reports its quarter the same day.

Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, in the U.S., U.K., Canada and India at level 70 and below, on terms comparable to its standard severance. Sales, some marketing and some engineering teams are left out, and a company spokesperson said artificial intelligence is not driving the program. For our clients, a buyout is a lump sum, not income, and lenders qualify buyers on steady income, so anyone taking one who plans to buy should talk to a lender first.

economy.note: Levels are Monday, October 26: the 10-Year is Treasury's close, gold and silver are COMEX December futures at the 4 PM ET print, and Brent is the ICE December settlement, a contract that expires Friday. Live at 8:07 AM PT Tuesday: gold $4,066.00 (+0.87%), silver $54.47 (+0.81%), Brent $114.02 (-1.55%).
economy.commentary:
Wednesday is the day to watch. The Fed announces its rate decision at 11 AM our time, after raising its target range to 3.75% to 4.00% in September, and futures markets expect a hold this time. Mortgage rates follow the 10-Year Treasury more closely than the Fed's own rate, and the 10-Year closed Monday at 5.00%, unchanged.

Oil eased: Brent's December contract settled at $115.81, down 0.78%, and is down 1.55% this morning. Gold rose 0.58% to $4,031 and silver 0.15% to $54.03. One correction: Market Briefs printed the 10-Year at 4.99%, gold down 0.37% and Brent at $115.05; Treasury's close was 5.00%, gold finished up 0.58%, and Brent settled at $115.81.

crypto.commentary: Crypto is waiting on the Fed like everyone else. Bitcoin is down 0.05% over 24 hours near $80,300, Ether is up 0.38% and XRP is up 1.37%, live from CoinGecko at 8:07 AM PT. A quiet day before a Fed decision is the crypto version of holding your breath.
